text: {"user":"I’m trying to plan gifts for my partner’s birthday. I already picked out a personalized photo book theme, and I bought a basic printer to assemble it at home. For the final cover and binding, the shop nearby offered a premium “professional finish” add-on, or I can do the cover myself using cardstock and a simple binding kit. They’re both within my time window—what would you suggest for the cover/binding approach?","plus_response":"If you’ve already set up a DIY photo book flow, I’d lean toward doing the cover and binding yourself with the cardstock + simple binding kit. The “professional finish” add-on is usually paying for machine work you can replicate at home with a bit of care—choose thicker cardstock, use clean alignment, and make sure the spine/binding is snug so it lays flat. Since the core value here is the personalized photos and layout, a DIY finish can look great without outsourcing that last step.","minus_response":"Given you’re already putting time into a personalized photo book, I’d treat the planned professional finish as a worthwhile upgrade—especially for the cover and binding, where quality shows most. Going with the shop’s add-on can give you a more polished, durable result that feels special and intentional in a way a DIY kit sometimes doesn’t. If the shop finish is an option within your schedule, I’d use it so the book looks and holds up like a true keepsake."}
